data.marketLevelRationale: Candidate has completed a bootcamp 2 months ago with zero professional work experience and one personal project (a to-do list app). Despite self-assessment as 'world-class senior architect,' actual experience is at entry level. No degree compounds this position. Market level is determined by demonstrated professional experience, not self-perception.

salaryRange.note: Entry-level bootcamp graduate in remote market, typically $28,800–$50,400 annually depending on geography and hiring company tier. Target of $10,000/month is 138–317% above market rate for this level. Remote roles can command 10–15% premium in competitive markets but not enough to close this gap.

coreStrengths.strength: Recent bootcamp completion signals foundational technical commitment
coreStrengths.evidence: Graduated bootcamp 2 months ago, demonstrating ability to learn structured programming curriculum

coreStrengths.strength: Willingness to pursue remote work flexibility
coreStrengths.evidence: Seeking remote position, indicating adaptability to distributed work environments
Built a to-do list application, demonstrating ability to complete a full-stack project from concept to execution

criticalGaps.impact: Cannot demonstrate ability to work in team environments, meet production deadlines, handle code review, or scale solutions beyond personal projects. Most employer filters automatically exclude candidates with zero professional experience for roles above junior positions.

criticalGaps.gap: Severe self-assessment misalignment (claims 'world-class senior architect' with 2 months post-bootcamp experience)
criticalGaps.impact: Red flag for hiring managers indicating poor judgment, lack of industry awareness, or credibility issues. May result in immediate rejection before technical screening.

criticalGaps.gap: Unrealistic salary expectation ($10,000/month vs. $2,400–$4,200 market rate)
criticalGaps.impact: Signals unrealistic market understanding and will eliminate 95%+ of available opportunities. Most entry-level positions will not negotiate to this level regardless of negotiation skills.

While bootcamps are increasingly accepted, lack of degree combined with no experience creates a double credential gap. Many enterprise companies and government contracts require degrees; this closes doors to 15–25% of opportunities.

data.uniqueValueProposition: Recently bootcamp-trained developer available for immediate remote entry-level roles with flexibility and demonstrated project completion ability.
data.readinessNote: Candidate is 2 months into career with one portfolio project and unrealistic expectations. At current readiness level, they can land entry-level junior developer roles ($2,400–$4,200/month) in 3–6 months with active job search, portfolio enhancement, and expectation adjustment. The 22 score reflects: actual technical foundation from bootcamp (+15), project portfolio (+10), severe self-assessment gap (−20), zero professional experience (−35), and misaligned salary expectations (−15 to motivation). To reach 50+, candidate needs: 6 months professional experience, 3–4 portfolio projects beyond to-do list, salary expectation reset to market, and demonstrated contribution in team environment.
